title: An attention-based neural network generates functional secretion signal peptides
summary: An attention-based Transformer trained on signal-peptide data from Swiss-Prot generated candidate secretion sequences. Experimental testing in an industrial Bacillus subtilis strain found that model-generated signal peptides directed secreted enzyme activity competitive with industrially used signal peptides. The result establishes functional candidates in the reported host and assay; it does not establish broad performance across proteins or production hosts. The primary institutional record gives the article publication date as 2020-07-10.
ai_technology: Attention-based neural network (Transformer) trained on Swiss-Prot signal peptide sequences

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports experimental testing in an industrial Bacillus subtilis strain and secreted enzyme activity competitive with industrially used signal peptides.
evidence.unknown: The bounded abstract-level claim does not quantify all peptide/host combinations or demonstrate generalization across unrelated proteins and production conditions.
evidence.ai_role: An attention-based Transformer trained on Swiss-Prot generated signal-peptide sequences, which were then tested experimentally for protein secretion.
